transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I came in because I’ve been feeling low for a really long time. Most mornings I wake up and it’s already there, like this heavy gray feeling, and it follows me through the day, even when I’m at the clinic.
Has this low mood been there most days for at least two years?
Yeah. It’s been most days for about two years and a couple months now. I think it really started after the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches when your low mood went away completely for as long as two months?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a time where it was completely gone for that long, but I haven’t exactly been keeping track like that.
During this period, have there been times when your depression became much worse and lasted at least two weeks?
I’m not sure. I mean, it feels pretty consistently bad, but I don’t know if I can clearly point to a two-week stretch where it was suddenly much worse than the rest.
Did your low mood start within about three months after the staffing changes at the clinic?
Yeah, I think so. It started around when the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place. It’s been going on about two years and two months now.
At any point in the past two years, did you have a stretch of two months when you did not feel depressed at all?

No, I don’t think so. It’s been pretty much there the whole time — I wake up already feeling low, like this heavy gray feeling is on me, and it follows me through the day. I can’t remember two months where it was just gone.
During this time, have you often had low self-esteem?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed that as a main thing. I mean, I feel bad a lot, but I don’t know if I’d call it low self-esteem exactly.
During this time, have you often felt hopeless?

Yeah. I think that’s been there a lot. I keep feeling like… this is just what my life is now — random hours, always behind, never having enough money or energy to get back to school or do anything better. It’s hard to see it changing.
During this time, have you often had low energy?

Yeah, definitely. Even if I sleep in or have a day off, I still feel worn out. At work, after rooming patients and trying to catch up on charts, I’m just drained. By the time I get home, I don’t have much left for laundry or playing basketball or even messing with my electronics stuff.
During this time, have you often had trouble making decisions?

Yeah, I do. It’s more like I can’t think clearly sometimes. At work I’ll be looking at a patient’s intake screen and have to reread the same line over and over. I’ve also missed little things, like medication doses, or I’ll forget what I was about to ask them next.
During this time, have you often had a poor appetite or been overeating?
I don’t think that’s been a big thing for me. My eating is kind of irregular with work sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a major change in appetite or overeating.
Has this low mood been making it hard for you to function in your daily life?

Yeah, it has. At work, my supervisor put me on a performance plan because I was making too many mistakes with intakes. And outside of work I’m barely keeping up with anything. I’ve stopped showing up for basketball, and I don’t really finish the little electronics projects I used to do with friends. It’s like I don’t have enough in me to handle work and anything else.
During the past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you felt markedly more depressed than your usual baseline?

Yeah… I mean, it’s hard to separate out because it’s been going on so long. Most days I wake up already feeling low, like there’s this heavy gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic, and it kind of stays with me through the day. So I’m not sure about a clear two-week stretch being different from my normal, because my normal has been pretty low.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried a lot during this time?
I don’t know… not especially anxious, I guess. I worry about stuff here and there, but I haven’t noticed anxiety being the main thing. It’s more just feeling low most of the time.
Are the staffing problems and rotating schedule at the clinic still going on?
Yeah, they’re still going on. It’s been like this for about two years and a couple months now, since the staffing changed and my schedule started rotating all over the place.
If the problems at the clinic suddenly got better, do you think you would still feel depressed?

I think… yeah, I probably still would. The clinic stuff makes it harder, but even before I get there, I wake up feeling low, like this heavy gray feeling is already there. It follows me through most of the day.
During this time, was there ever a two-week period when you lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I’ve had times where I didn’t feel like doing much, but I don’t know if it was almost everything, most of the day, every day for two straight weeks. I’d have to think about it more.
During this time, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you had trouble sleeping nearly every night?
I’m not really sure. My sleep hasn’t been great at times, but I don’t know if it was nearly every night for a full two weeks. I’d have to think about that.
Was there ever a period lasting at least two weeks when you had almost no interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know for sure. I’ve had times where I really didn’t feel like doing much, but whether it was almost no interest or pleasure for two full weeks straight… I’m not sure.
During the past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your depression was clearly worse than your usual level?

I’m not sure. It’s kind of been low for so long that it’s hard for me to tell what counts as clearly worse. I’ve had rough stretches, but I don’t know if I can say it was a full two weeks and definitely worse than usual.
